collection_title: Records of the President of Harvard University, Abbott Lawrence Lowell, 1909-1933
lead_basis: Batch119 established that British officials intended the no-passport decision to be communicated to the President of Harvard and that Harvard had already publicly institutionalized Bertrand Russell's 1916-17 teaching plan. Harvard's official HOLLIS finding aid identifies UAI 5.160.x as the President's Office records of Abbott Lawrence Lowell, 1909-1933, documenting almost every aspect of his administration; General Correspondence has a separate index, and the physical folder-list inventory contains a 1914-1917 series.
person_or_network_pivot: Abbott Lawrence Lowell / James Haughton Woods / Bertrand Russell / Cecil Spring Rice / British Embassy / Harvard philosophy appointment and passport notification, 1916
expected_material: President's incoming/outgoing correspondence, appointment and curricular administration, British Embassy or Foreign Office communications, copies/routing records concerning Russell's Harvard engagement and inability to travel
next_query: use the General Correspondence index first, then the 1914-1917 physical folder list; search Russell, Bertrand, Woods, James Haughton, Spring Rice, British Embassy, passport, philosophy, appointment, lectures, and Harvard President; capture any cross-reference before requesting physical folder
notes: This is a strong provenance-shaped reciprocal lead, not proof that any specific Russell/Spring Rice document survives in UAI 5.160.x. HOLLIS states that the folder lists are secondary to the index and that the 1914-1917 physical series is not alphabetically arranged, so absence of a literal Russell folder title would not be an absence result.
